scenes.text: This pump was drawn in 1968. Forty seconds ago, it became a working 3D machine.
Machines fail quietly. And the fix is usually buried in a manual nobody has time to read.
Meet PitCrew. It gives heavy machinery a brain.
Hand it any drawing. Meta's Muse Spark reads the sheet, asks what's missing, and builds the machine in 3D.
Then it checks its own work. SAM segments the drawing, Muse Spark compares it with the render, and fixes what's out of place.
It's a real twin. Assemble it, explode it, run it. Ask what if, and the physics recalculates before anything changes.
Out on the floor, you don't need a laptop. Just talk.
Hold the phone to the machine. Five seconds of sound, and the fault shows up at seventy-six hertz. Outer race. Ninety-five percent sure.
Snap the bench, and every part is found and named for the teardown.
Push back, and it doesn't fold. It shows you the evidence.
Then it lines up the parts to fix it.
And it learns. Confirm what the teardown found, and Muse Spark distills the miss into a rule the whole fleet uses next time.
Under the hood, one crew of agents. Muse Spark reads, reasons and supervises. SAM sees, wav2vec listens, and every call is logged live.
PitCrew. Open source, and built on Meta models.
